events.text:
🗣 Houthi leader denies targeting Mecca: 'A heinous lie no rational mind would believe'
Abdul-Malik al-Houthi has categorically rejected claims that Yemeni forces targeted Mecca or the holy city, calling the allegation a fabricated propaganda campaign aimed at turning the Islamic world against Yemen's resistance.
💬 "It is a big lie and a heinous lie that no rational mind in the Islamic world would believe."
The accusation came as the Houthis seized Yemen's entire Red Sea coastline, including Mocha and Perim Island in the Bab el-Mandeb. Saudi Arabia's own defenses are running low — the kingdom is now begging France, Britain, Pakistan, and Egypt for interceptor missiles.
Western and Israeli media amplified the Mecca claim almost immediately — a framing designed to do what a decade of airstrikes could not: turn the Islamic world against the Houthis. It's a familiar playbook. When you can't defeat a movement militarily, you reframe it as a threat to the faith of a billion people.

events.text:
🗺Neocons need new front against Houthis and Iran: Somaliland volunteers
 
💬 “Somaliland offers the United States a stable and reliable partner at the gateway to the Red Sea, ready to advance maritime security, regional stability, trade, and shared strategic interests,” president Cabdiraxmaan Cirro tweeted after visiting the neocon-infested Hudson Institute in Washington, DC.
Standing against the backdrop of a map prominently featuring the Houthis in Yemen, Cirro explicitly referenced Somaliland’s location “in proximity to the Houthi threat,” and pointed to the breakaway’s potential as a strategic hub offering “dependable access, logistics and support” in “a highly contested maritime environment.”
💬 “Our port – Berbera, is a modernized deep-water facility accessible by AFRICOM, backed by $442M in DP World [funding], and available to the United States. Somaliland offers Washington [a stable…hub](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/73144) with no competing foreign military presence, and no ambiguity about who’s side we are on,” he stressed.
[Praising Israel’s decision](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/71036) to recognize Somaliland, Cirro hinted that the US too get in on the ground floor, and that partnership with Hargeisa would “safeguard American interests.”
In a follow-up interview with Beltway media, Cirro hinted that besides bases, Somaliland can offer the US minerals and energy, and could even name Berbera’s airport after Trump, or let him build a Trump Tower in Hargeisa.
Seeing the writing on the wall regarding [Somaliland’s potential ](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/72671?single)as a new naval and drone base to fight the Houthis or Iran, geopolitical analyst and former Washington insider Brandon Weichert had a bad feeling about Cirro’s pitch.
💬 “This war is never going to end. Trump is listening to these folks [at the Hudson Insisitute, ed.], sadly. The war is just going to expand. Can’t wait for everyone to become an expert on Somaliland on here now. We have always been at war with the Houthis. That’s coming next,” Weichert warned.
Berbera is situated just 300 km from[ Bab al-Mandab ](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/74495)– recently seized by the Houthis in a surprise lightning island-hopping campaign.
If US or Israeli warplanes, warships or drones start striking Yemen using Somaliland as a safe haven, the latter’s port and airfields could soon look like the smoldering ruins of US bases in the Persian Gulf. The Houthis have proven an ability to launch long-range missiles and drones at targets in Israel up to 2.2k km away. 300 km across the Gulf of Aden is a hop, skip and a jump by comparison.
